hypotheses.text: The primary clinical discovery cohorts defining Popov-Chang syndrome (Chang et al. 2019 and Popov et al.) describe cardiofaciocutaneous (CFC)-like features, including distinctive craniofacial dysmorphism and ectodermal involvement, in at least 50% of assessed patients rather than pure non-syndromic intellectual disability.
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifying whether the foundational cohort phenotypes resemble a RASopathy/CFC-like phenotype versus non-syndromic neurodevelopmental delay determines which specific HPO terms (e.g., HP:0001580 abnormal skin morphology, HP:0000316 hypertelorism) have high diagnostic sensitivity in clinical cohorts.

evidence.text: Chang et al. investigated a YWHAZ variant associated with cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome that activates the RAF-ERK pathway and discussed relating clinical phenotypes to YWHAZ variation alongside other CFC syndrome genes.

source.title: A YWHAZ variant associated with cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome activates the RAF-ERK pathway
source.quote: relate clinical phenotypes to YWHAZ variation. … patients with variants in YWHAZ, our data, combined with the evidence that variations in other genes associated with CFC syndrome

evidence.text: GeneCards documents that YWHAZ is associated with both Popov-Chang Syndrome and Autosomal Dominant Non-Syndromic Intellectual Disability.

source.title: YWHAZ Gene
source.quote: Diseases associated with YWHAZ include Popov-Chang Syndrome and Autosomal Dominant Non-Syndromic Intellectual Disability.

hypotheses.text: Pathogenic variants clustering at amino acid residue Ser230 of YWHAZ (such as p.Ser230Trp and frameshift c.688_689insAT / p.Ser230TyrfsTer44) represent recurrent hotspot alleles responsible for greater than 30% of all reported Popov-Chang syndrome cases in literature series.
hypotheses.rationale: OMIM and ClinVar independently highlight distinct variants at Ser230 (a missense substitution and a 2-bp insertion frameshift), suggesting codon 230 is an allele hotspot where exact phenotypic numerators can be compared across missense versus truncating variants.

hypotheses.text: Refractory epileptic encephalopathy (HP:0200134) is present in fewer than 15% of molecularly confirmed Popov-Chang syndrome patients, distinguishing it from classical developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
hypotheses.rationale: Reviews on epileptic encephalopathies emphasize the expansion of genetic testing to variable phenotypes; clarifying whether epilepsy is a core or minor finding in YWHAZ cohorts enables clinicians to discriminate Popov-Chang syndrome from severe epileptic channelopathies and YWHAG-associated disorders.

evidence.text: Hebbar and Mefford describe phenotype expansions across large cohorts tested for severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathies, noting that over 50% of DEE patients remain without a diagnosis.

source.title: Recent advances in epilepsy genomics and genetic testing
